units.text: 4. Taking into account historical and other local traditions and the possession of honorary titles of the USSR and the Russian Federation, individual settlements forming part of a municipality may, in accordance with the municipal charter, have official settlement symbols.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 8

units.locator: Chapter 2. Territorial foundations of the organization of local self-government
units.text: Chapter 2. Territorial foundations of the organization of local self-government
units.label: Chapter 2. Territorial foundations of the organization of local self-government

units.text: Article 9. Types of municipalities
units.label: Art. 9

units.text: 1. A municipality is a public-law entity established in a territory with a permanently resident population, within whose boundaries local self-government is exercised by the population directly and/or through local self-government bodies.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 9

units.text: 2. Local self-government is exercised in the following types of municipalities:
units.label: Part 2 Art. 9

units.text: 1) urban okrug;
units.label: Point 1 Part 2 Art. 9

units.text: 2) municipal okrug;
units.label: Point 2 Part 2 Art. 9

units.text: 3) intracity municipality of a city of federal significance.
units.label: Point 3 Part 2 Art. 9

units.text: 3. An urban okrug is a municipality whose territory includes one or more cities and/or other urban settlements that are not themselves municipalities and in which at least two thirds of the urban okrug’s population reside. An urban okrug may also include the territories of rural settlements that are not themselves municipalities and territories intended for the development of the urban okrug’s social, transport and other infrastructure. The combined area of the territories of rural settlements and territories intended for the development of the urban okrug’s social, transport and other infrastructure included in the urban okrug may not be two or more times the area of the territories of cities and/or other urban settlements included in the urban okrug. The population density in an urban okrug must be at least five times the average population density in the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 9

units.text: 4. A municipal okrug is a municipality whose territory includes one or more rural settlements that are not themselves municipalities. A municipal okrug may also include the territories of urban settlements that are not themselves municipalities and territories intended for the development of the municipal okrug’s social, transport and other infrastructure. The combined area of the territories of rural settlements and territories intended for the development of the municipal okrug’s social, transport and other infrastructure included in the municipal okrug must be at least twice the area of the urban settlements included in the municipal okrug.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 9

units.text: 5. An intracity municipality of a city of federal significance is a municipality located in the territory of a city of federal significance.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 9

units.text: 6. The type of a municipality is determined by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation in accordance with the requirements of this Article.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 9

units.text: 7. In constituent entities of the Russian Federation having socioeconomic, historical, ethnic and other particular features, the organization of local self-government may be regulated taking into account special arrangements that allow the territorial organization of local self-government established by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation as of the date this Federal Law enters into force to be retained, with local self-government exercised in the types of municipalities specified in points 1 and 2 of part 2 of this Article and/or in municipalities forming a two-tier system of local self-government (settlement municipalities (rural and urban) and municipal raions).
units.label: Part 7 Art. 9

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.label: Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 1. The territory of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation is divided among municipal and urban okrugs, and, in constituent entities of the Russian Federation that are cities of federal significance, among intracity municipalities of the city of federal significance.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 2. The territory of a municipality must lie wholly within the territory of a single constituent entity of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 3. The territories of municipalities are determined taking into account historical and other local traditions.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 4. The territory of a municipality includes land irrespective of its form of ownership or designated use.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 5. Laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation establishing and changing municipal boundaries must contain a list of the settlements included in the territories of those municipalities.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 6. The territory of a settlement must be wholly included in the territory of a municipality.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 7. The territory of a municipality may not form part of the territory of another municipality.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 8. A city or settlement located in an urban okrug that shares a boundary with a municipal okrug may be regarded as the administrative center of that municipal okrug.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 9. Municipal boundaries are generally established taking into account transport accessibility that enables residents of all settlements within them to travel to their administrative centers and back within a working day. Under laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, these requirements may be inapplicable to municipalities in areas with low population density and in remote and hard-to-reach localities.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 10. Areas with low population density comprise the territories of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and of individual municipalities within constituent entities of the Russian Federation where population density is less than one third of the average population density in the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 10

units.locator: Article 10. Principles of the territorial organization of local self-government
units.text: 11. In constituent entities of the Russian Federation where traditional forms of transhumant livestock farming have historically developed, the territories and boundaries of municipalities are established taking into account the legislation of the constituent entity regulating the procedure for determining territories and using land for transhumant livestock farming, and the patterns of population settlement in those territories.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 10

units.text: Article 11. Municipal boundaries
units.label: Art. 11

units.text: 1. The boundaries of municipal territories are established and changed by laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation in accordance with the requirements of this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 11

units.text: 2. The boundaries of a municipality are changed by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation at the initiative of the population, local self-government bodies, state authorities of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation or federal state authorities, in accordance with this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 11

units.text: 3. The population’s initiative to change municipal boundaries is exercised in accordance with the procedure established by a federal law and a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation adopted in accordance with it for proposing a local referendum.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 11

units.text: 4. An initiative of local self-government bodies or state authorities to change municipal boundaries is formalized by decisions of the relevant local self-government bodies or state authorities.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 11

units.text: 5. A law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation changing municipal boundaries must not enter into force during an election campaign for a local self-government body of that municipality or during a local referendum campaign.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 11

units.text: 6. Municipal boundaries are changed with the consent of the populations of the municipalities, expressed by the representative bodies of the respective municipalities.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 11

units.text: Article 12. Transformation of municipalities
units.label: Art. 12

units.text: 1. The transformation of municipalities means the merger of municipalities, the division of municipalities or a change in the type of a municipality.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 12

units.text: 2. Municipalities are transformed by laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation at the initiative of the population, local self-government bodies, state authorities of constituent entities of the Russian Federation or federal state authorities, in accordance with this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 12

units.text: 3. The population’s initiative to transform a municipality is exercised in accordance with the procedure established by a federal law and a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation adopted in accordance with it for proposing a local referendum.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 12

units.text: 4. An initiative of local self-government bodies or state authorities to transform a municipality is formalized by decisions of the relevant local self-government bodies or state authorities.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 12

units.text: 5. A law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation transforming a municipality must not enter into force during an election campaign for a local self-government body of that municipality or during a local referendum campaign.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 12

units.text: 6. Municipalities are merged with the consent of the population, expressed by the representative bodies of each of the merging municipalities. Each of the merged municipalities loses its status as a municipality.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 12

units.text: 7. A municipality is divided so as to create two or more municipalities taking into account the opinion of the population, expressed by the representative body of the municipality concerned.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 12

units.text: 8. A municipality’s type is changed from an urban okrug to a municipal okrug if the urban okrug ceases to meet the requirements concerning the proportion of the population residing in cities and/or other urban settlements and the area of the urban okrug, or the population density in the urban okrug, provided for in part 3 of Article 9 of this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 12

units.text: 9. A municipality’s type is changed from a municipal okrug to an urban okrug if the municipal okrug ceases to meet the requirement concerning the area of the municipal okrug provided for in part 4 of Article 9 of this Federal Law, provided that it meets the requirements concerning the proportion of the population residing in cities and/or other urban settlements, territorial area and population density provided for in part 3 of Article 9 of this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 12

units.text: 10. The transformation of municipalities entails the creation of newly formed municipalities in the cases provided for in parts 6 and 7 of this Article.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 12

units.locator: Chapter 3. Organizational foundations of local self-government
units.text: Chapter 3. Organizational foundations of local self-government
units.label: Chapter 3. Organizational foundations of local self-government

units.text: Article 13. Local self-government bodies
units.label: Art. 13

units.text: 1. Local self-government bodies mean bodies elected directly by the population or established by the representative body of a municipality and vested with their own powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 13

units.text: 2. Local self-government bodies are formed by citizens directly in municipal elections or indirectly through deputies elected in municipal elections.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 13

units.text: 3. The head of a municipality, the head of the local administration and other local self-government officials may, in accordance with the municipal charter, acquire and exercise property and other rights and duties and appear in court on behalf of the municipality without a power of attorney.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 13

units.text: 4. Local self-government bodies vested with the rights of a legal entity in accordance with this Federal Law and the municipal charter are municipal treasury-funded institutions established to perform administrative functions and are subject to state registration as legal entities in accordance with federal law. The representative body of a municipality and the local administration, as legal entities, operate in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Code of the Russian Federation on treasury-funded institutions.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 13

units.text: 5. The grounds for state registration of local self-government bodies as legal entities are the municipal charter and a decision to establish the relevant local self-government body with the rights of a legal entity.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 13

units.text: 6. In the absence of a municipal charter, the grounds for state registration of local self-government bodies as legal entities are:
units.label: Part 6 Art. 13

units.text: 1) for the representative body of a municipality, the minutes of a meeting of that representative body containing a decision to vest it with the rights of a legal entity;
units.label: Point 1 Part 6 Art. 13

units.text: 2) for other local self-government bodies, a decision of the representative body of the municipality to establish the relevant local self-government body with the rights of a legal entity.
units.label: Point 2 Part 6 Art. 13

units.text: 7. The grounds for state registration of bodies of the local administration as legal entities are a decision of the representative body of the municipality to establish the relevant body in the form of a municipal treasury-funded institution and that representative body’s approval of regulations governing it, upon submission by the head of the local administration.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 13

units.text: 8. Organizational and logistical support for the activities of local self-government bodies is funded exclusively from the own revenues of the budgets of the respective municipalities, except in the cases provided for by this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 13

units.text: 9. Local self-government bodies and local self-government officials bear liability provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation, including where they violate the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal constitutional laws, federal laws, the constitution (charter) or laws of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation or the municipal charter, and where those bodies and officials improperly exercise individual state powers delegated to them.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 13

units.text: 10. Elections to local self-government bodies of a newly formed municipality are held within the time limits provided for by the legislation on elections and referendums, unless otherwise provided by federal constitutional laws.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 13

units.text: 11. Until the local self-government bodies of a newly formed municipality are formed, powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in that newly formed municipality are exercised in the relevant territories by the local self-government bodies that exercised powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in those territories on the day the newly formed municipality was created.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 13

units.text: 12. Municipal legal acts adopted by local self-government bodies that, on the day a newly formed municipality was created, exercised powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in the relevant territories remain in force insofar as they do not conflict with federal laws and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation, constitutions (charters), laws and other regulatory legal acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, or municipal legal acts of the local self-government bodies of the newly formed municipality.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 13

units.text: 13. In accordance with their competence, the local self-government bodies of a newly formed municipality are the legal successors of the local self-government bodies that, on the day the newly formed municipality was created, exercised powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in the relevant territory, in relations with state authorities of the Russian Federation, state authorities of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, local self-government bodies, individuals and legal entities. Matters of legal succession must be regulated by municipal legal acts of the newly formed municipality.
units.label: Part 13 Art. 13

units.text: 14. Until municipal legal acts of the newly formed municipality regulate matters of legal succession in respect of bodies of local administrations, municipal institutions, enterprises and organizations previously established by or with the participation of the local self-government bodies that, on the day the newly formed municipality was created, exercised powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in the relevant territory, those bodies of local administrations, municipal institutions, enterprises and organizations continue their activities while retaining their previous organizational and legal form.
units.label: Part 14 Art. 13

units.locator: Article 14. Structure of local self-government bodies
units.text: Article 14. Structure of local self-government bodies
units.label: Art. 14

units.locator: Article 14. Structure of local self-government bodies
units.text: 1. The structure of local self-government bodies consists of the representative body of the municipality, the head of the municipality, the local administration (the municipality’s executive and administrative body), the municipality’s control and accounts body, and other bodies provided for by the municipal charter and having their own powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 14

units.locator: Article 14. Structure of local self-government bodies
units.text: 2. The structure of local self-government bodies must include the representative body of the municipality, the head of the municipality and the local administration.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 14
